name: Trace-Carrier and Ample-Prefix Equivalence
statement: An ample family has an ample-prefix ordering, equivalently a reverse corner peeling, if and only if it admits an acyclic trace-carrier scheme.
proof: A corner-peeling order has a bijective first-loss map on the shattered supports. Assign each support to the concept at its loss time and choose the last later representative of every competing trace; every carrier and protector arc points forward. Conversely, any topological ordering of an acyclic scheme makes the carrier of each support its unique first-loss concept, so the first-loss map is bijective. The first-loss criterion makes every suffix ample and hence makes the order a corner peeling; reversing it gives an ample-prefix ordering.
